entities.name: Perisophia
entities.description: A Meletian philosopher and teacher who leads her students in a discussion of identity and, in a dream, speaks with the god Ephara.

entities.name: Ephara
entities.description: The god of city-states, whose voice tells Perisophia in the void that war is coming and that a tyrant tears at the threshold of the world.

entities.name: Kyrios
entities.description: A student of Perisophia who argues that the leonin cub remains a leonin.

entities.name: Samia
entities.description: A student of Perisophia who has read Dekatia's Observations and asks about the Returned and the eidolons.

entities.name: Rhytho
entities.description: A student of Perisophia who argues that identity cannot be given by an outside observer.

entities.name: Melia
entities.description: A student of Perisophia who cites Phelos on identity.

entities.name: Salis
entities.description: A student of Perisophia who raises the story of Matatios.

entities.name: Athreos
entities.description: The god who helps the dead pass into the Underworld.

entities.name: Erebos
entities.description: The god who watches over the dead in the eternally gray Underworld.

entities.name: Mogis
entities.description: A god whose seed Perisophia senses lurking in every living soul.

entities.name: Matatios
entities.description: A figure from a story who met himself through overwhelming self-infatuation.

entities.name: Phelos
entities.description: A thinker cited as stating that identity is the condition of being oneself over time.

entities.name: Dekatia
entities.description: The author of Observations, which discusses the Returned and eidolons.

entities.name: The Returned
entities.description: Dead people who escaped the Underworld and lost all identity, becoming faceless.

entities.name: Eidolon
entities.description: The spectral embodiment of the lost identity of a Returned, without agency and never reunited with it.

entities.name: Leonin
entities.description: A race used in the hypothetical example of a cub raised by wolves.

entities.name: Setessans
entities.description: People of a polis that Perisophia says kills truth with arrows.

entities.name: Akroans
entities.description: People of a polis that Perisophia says kills truth with swords.

entities.name: Meletians
entities.description: People of a polis that Perisophia says kills truth with their minds.

entities.name: Theros
entities.description: The plane where the dead pass into the Underworld.

entities.name: Underworld
entities.description: The eternally gray realm without sun or night where the dead dwell under Erebos.

entities.name: Meletis
entities.description: Ephara's polis, where Perisophia teaches in the Forum.

events.summary: Perisophia opens a lesson in Meletis by asking her students what identity is, using the example of a leonin cub raised by wolves.
events.quote: "What is identity? What makes us who we are?"

events.summary: Perisophia urges her students to dwell in the mystery rather than hastily answering.
events.quote: Dwell in the mystery for a bit and see what arises.

events.summary: Melia cites Phelos, and Perisophia presses whether identity can be an object of knowledge.
events.quote: Can you know yourself? Can your identity be an object of knowledge, or is it something entirely different?

events.summary: Samia asks about the Returned and eidolons, and Perisophia explains that they lack the capacity for an identity.
events.quote: It would appear that the Returned and the eidolons lack the capacity for an identity.

events.summary: Salis raises the story of Matatios, and Perisophia warns that Matatios only met himself and did not become aware of himself.
events.quote: Matatios did not become aware of himself, he only met himself.

events.summary: Perisophia ends the lesson by saying that identity lives in the moment and that each person is the architect of it.
events.quote: Identity is not in the past, nor does it dwell in the future. It lives in the moment.

events.summary: In a dream-vision in a void of stars, Ephara asks Perisophia about Meletis and warns that war is coming and a tyrant tears at the threshold of the world.
events.quote: War is coming. A tyrant tears at the threshold of our world and yours

events.summary: Perisophia vows to speak only words that uplift the human mind and soul with her dying breath.
events.quote: With my dying breath I will speak only words that uplift the human mind and soul.

relations.quote: "So, what is the nature of identity?" Rhytho asked.

relations.note: Ephara calls Meletis her city and Perisophia reports to her.
relations.quote: "How is my city?" The voice of Ephara echoed into the void.

relations.note: He helps the dead pass into the Underworld, from which the Returned escaped.
relations.quote: they pass into the Underworld with the aid of the god Athreos, the River Guide.

relations.note: He watches over the dead in the Underworld.
relations.quote: They dwell in this eternally gray realm without sun or night under the watch of Erebos, god of the Underworld.

relations.note: Each Returned has a severed eidolon, and they are never reunited.
relations.quote: The Returned and its severed eidolon are never reunited, nor are they aware of one another's existence.
